title: Felodipine in WWOX-LoF
summary: A comparison of native Tau clearance and altered phosphorylation.

graph.evidence: Mouse aggregate burden fell and a separate Tau model changed soluble phospho-Tau.
graph.inference: A lower phospho-Tau signal leaves cargo turnover unresolved.
graph.hypothesis: WWOX loss may impair disposal or increase the production of phosphorylated Tau.
graph.experiment: Track old Tau at matched calcium current and test axonal function.

evidence: The published Huntington mouse workbook shows 28.2% and 25.9% lower normalized aggregate-positive cells in piriform and motor cortex. Both directions survive paired batch omissions.
inference: The cortical α-synuclein worksheet repeats density values. PS19 soluble phospho-Tau fell, but WWOX Tau turnover remains unmeasured.
hypothesis: Felodipine may accelerate lysosomal turnover or alter calcium-dependent phosphorylation. The two routes can change the same terminal marker.
experiment: Compare with an independent intervention matched on early L-type current. Measure decay of old Tau across cells and medium, phosphosite occupancy, lysosomal dependence and axonal transport.
limits: The retained mouse phenotype cohort averaged 46.84 nM total plasma. Pediatric free brain exposure remains unknown. Keep felodipine as a conditional laboratory comparator.
